Free to start, free to publish, no developer needed. See how Kodely fits a volunteer-run budget.", "targetKeyword": "ai website builder for nonprofits", "category": "Personas", "bodyHtml": "

Your website is not the problem you have time for

Most nonprofits do not have a marketing budget, let alone a web development budget. Whoever updates the website, if anyone does, is usually a volunteer board member or the executive director squeezing it in between grant reports. Hiring an agency, or even a freelance developer for a few hours, is a cost that is hard to justify when every dollar is earmarked for the mission. Yet the website still matters: it is often the first thing a potential donor, volunteer, or grant reviewer checks before deciding whether an organization is legitimate and active.

How Kodely fits a nonprofit budget and skill set

Kodely is a chat-based AI website builder. Describe your organization in plain English - the mission, the programs you run, who you serve, how people can help - and Kodely generates a real website: an actual Vite plus React 19, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS v4 application, built from real component files, not a static mockup or a locked-down template. You watch a live preview render the app as it is built. When something needs to change later, you say so in chat and Kodely edits the real components. No developer, no ticket, no waiting on someone's volunteer hours but your own.

Publishing is one click and it is free: your site goes live at a public yourorg.kodely.site address immediately, with no hosting bill and no credit card required to start. Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change breaks something, rolling back costs nothing extra. And if a volunteer developer ever wants to look under the hood, Kodely's code view lets anyone see and copy the actual generated source files.

Three ways nonprofits are actually using this

  • A mission and programs site. An about page, program pages describing what you actually run, an impact section, and a contact page. This is the site most nonprofits need most: something credible to link from a grant application, a social post, or a newsletter footer.
  • An event or fundraiser announcement page. A focused page for a gala, a 5k, or a giving-day campaign, with the date, location, and a clear call to action - built in an afternoon in the run-up to the event instead of weeks ahead of it.
  • A volunteer sign-up and contact page. A page explaining current volunteer needs with a way to reach out, whether that is an email address, a phone number, or a simple contact form, without needing a full scheduling system built in.

Be honest about donations

One thing Kodely will not do: process an actual donation. Ask it to build a Donate button or a donation section, and it will - a clear, well-placed call to action styled to match the rest of your site. But Kodely generates frontend code only. It does not build a backend, a database, or a payment integration. To actually accept money, you connect that Donate button to a real payment processor as a separate step - a Stripe donation link, or a platform built for nonprofits such as Donorbox. That is normal: most nonprofit sites, however they are built, lean on a dedicated donation platform rather than custom payment code, and it is worth budgeting a small amount of time to wire that connection up once your site is live.

Pricing in plain terms

Every new account starts with 750 free credits, no credit card required - enough to build and publish a real site and try out changes before spending anything. Credits are metered from the actual AI cost of generating your site, and a generation that fails to compile is never charged.

Start with what you can describe, not what you can code

You do not need a developer on the board and you do not need a redesign budget. You need to be able to describe your mission, your programs, and how people can help - Kodely handles the rest, from the first draft to a published, public site.
